definitions.explanation: A tree that retains its leaves throughout the year, continuously shedding and replacing them rather than losing them all at once.

examples.japanese: ⟦{松|まつ}→松：02256_matsu⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{常緑樹|じょうりょくじゅ}⟦なので→なので：noentry⟧⟦{冬|ふゆ}→冬：00623_fuyu⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦{緑|みどり}→緑：00970_midori⟧⟦です→です：09485_desu⟧。
examples.english: Pine is an evergreen, so it stays green in winter too.

examples.japanese: {常緑樹|じょうりょくじゅ}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{一年中|いちねんじゅう}→一年中：17104_ichinenjuu⟧⟦{葉|は}→葉：02241_ha⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦あります→ある：00006_aru⟧。
examples.english: Evergreen trees have leaves all year round.

examples.japanese: ⟦{庭|にわ}→庭：02239_niwa⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{常緑樹|じょうりょくじゅ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{植|う}えると→植える：01210_ueru⟧⟦{冬|ふゆ}→冬：00623_fuyu⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦{寂|さび}しくない→寂しい：00880_sabishii⟧。
examples.english: If you plant evergreens in the garden, it won't look bleak in winter.

notes:
{常緑樹|じょうりょくじゅ} - trees that remain green year-round. {常緑|じょうりょく} means evergreen and {樹|じゅ} means tree.

TYPES:
- ⟦{常緑針葉樹|じょうりょくしんようじゅ}→常緑針葉樹：noentry⟧ (evergreen conifers, e.g. pine, cedar)
- ⟦{常緑広葉樹|じょうりょくこうようじゅ}→常緑広葉樹：noentry⟧ (evergreen broadleaf, e.g. camellia, tea plant)

Common Japanese evergreens include ⟦{松|まつ}→松：02256_matsu⟧ (pine, a symbol of longevity), ⟦{杉|すぎ}→杉：03889_sugi⟧ (cedar), ⟦{椿|つばき}→椿：04401_tsubaki⟧ (camellia), ⟦{椎|しい}→椎：noentry⟧ (chinquapin), and ⟦{茶|ちゃ}→茶：03433_cha⟧ (tea plant).

RELATED WORDS:
- ⟦{落葉樹|らくようじゅ}→落葉樹：04961_rakuyouju⟧ (deciduous tree, opposite)
